Three we would run.

Built, deployed and screenshotted from the real page. Each takes the design from one review and the data from the other, so they differ only in the order of the same two ingredients: proof that we can help, and the request.

How to read it

Same page, three sequences

Every arm shows the same real providers from the Dallas pool and wears the same surface: warm white, one raspberry action, 17px system sans. So a difference between them is a difference in order, not in how much effort went into the page. That is what makes them comparable at roughly 150 visitors each.

The sharpest way to read the three is what the first screen asks of you: tap a provider, fill a form, or answer a question. Nothing else about them differs.

At that sample we can separate produces submissions from produces none — a true 3% arm shows zero about 1.6% of the time. We cannot rank two that both work. A one-submission gap is noise.

There is no control. Both reviews dropped it: at ~45 visits it could never have estimated lift. The cost, said plainly so nobody claims otherwise later — this tells us which new page is best, never that the redesign beat the old one.
